seoTitle: How to Cancel a Google Workspace Domain Alias
metaDescription: Learn how to safely cancel and deactivate a domain alias in Google Workspace in 2026, including DNS cleanup after removal.
intro: A domain alias added by mistake, or simply no longer needed, can clutter your Workspace setup if left in place. This guide walks through how to properly deactivate and remove a domain alias without disrupting your email or other Google services.

steps.heading: Understand what a domain alias does
steps.body: A domain alias lets users receive email at an alternate domain that routes to the same Workspace account as your primary domain.

steps.heading: Decide why you're removing it
steps.body: Common reasons include a domain added by mistake, restructuring your business, or simplifying your Workspace setup.

steps.heading: Access the Admin Console
steps.body: Sign in with an admin account and go to the Domains section where your primary domain and aliases are listed.

steps.heading: Remove or deactivate the alias
steps.body: Select the domain alias you want to remove and follow the prompts to deactivate it from your account.

steps.heading: Clean up DNS records afterward
steps.body: Once removed, update or delete any DNS records tied to that domain so it's fully disconnected from Google Workspace.

faq.question: What happens to emails sent to the alias after it's removed?
faq.answer: Once removed, the alias domain will no longer route mail to your Workspace account, so any emails sent there afterward won't be delivered.

faq.question: Why is the option to remove my domain alias greyed out?
faq.answer: This can happen if the alias is still actively used by users or services — check for dependencies before trying to remove it again.

faq.question: Do I need to update DNS records after removing an alias?
faq.answer: Yes, cleaning up DNS records tied to the alias domain prevents lingering configuration issues even after it's deactivated in Workspace.

faq.question: Can I remove a domain alias without affecting my primary domain?
faq.answer: Yes, removing an alias only affects that specific secondary domain and doesn't impact your primary domain's email or services.
